User request: Explain, in general, how canceling a meeting differs from deleting it from a calendar. I am not asking you to change any event.

content.text:
Short answer
- Canceling a meeting is an explicit, recorded action (usually by the organizer) that tells attendees the meeting will not happen and typically sends them a cancellation notice.  
- Deleting an event usually means removing it from a particular calendar view or copy; it may or may not notify other participants depending on who deletes it and the calendar system.

Key differences
- Who the action affects
  - Organizer cancels: notifies all attendees and updates their calendars (removes or marks the event as canceled).  
  - Attendee deletes: removes the event only from that attendee’s calendar; the organizer and other attendees are not notified.
- Notifications and communications
  - Cancel = a cancellation message is usually sent (so people know the meeting is off).  
  - Delete = may send no message (so others may still expect the meeting).
- Resources and reservations
  - Canceling generally releases any resources (rooms, equipment) reserved for the meeting.  
  - Deleting only your copy does not release shared resources unless the system receives a cancellation from the organizer.
- Record and auditability
  - Canceled events are often retained in calendars with a “canceled” status or an audit trail (useful for records).  
  - Deleted events may leave no record in that calendar; others’ calendars may still show the event.
- Recurring events and exceptions
  - Canceling can be applied to one occurrence or the whole series and will inform participants accordingly.  
  - Deleting one occurrence from your own calendar removes only your copy; deleting a series without sending a cancellation can leave attendees confused.
- Protocol-level difference (how calendar systems implement it)
  - Many calendaring protocols use a cancellation message (e.g., iCalendar METHOD:CANCEL or similar) to propagate a cancellation. Removing an event from a local calendar file or app without issuing that cancellation will not propagate it.

Practical implication
- If you are the meeting organizer and you want everyone to know the meeting is off and free up booked resources, use “Cancel meeting.”  
- If you are an attendee who simply doesn’t want the event on your calendar, deleting it from your own calendar is sufficient—but it won’t tell others the meeting is canceled.

Behavior can vary by calendar platform; the above describes common, general distinctions.
